mechanism: Replace 8-bit RGB and adversarial image synthesis with direct float spatiotemporal regression
compatibility: Preserves 153x1000x3 output and matched B0/B1 inputs
estimator_information: Ground motion; optional sparse sensors and mask
hypothesis: Float regression reduces amplitude shrinkage and peak underestimation
risk: May lose fine local texture or underfit spatial coupling
pass_rule: Lower physical RMSE without >2% peak degradation
innovation_claim: Possible: direct float full-field regression removes image quantization as a confounder; prove with physical-unit and peak ablations.

mechanism: Coordinate queries propagate masked sensor temporal features to every target node while a ground-motion operator supplies the sensor-free prior
compatibility: Same parameters for zero and real masks; no target truth in input
estimator_information: Ground motion; sensor coordinates; available sensor acceleration and mask
hypothesis: Coordinate-conditioned masked fusion improves unobserved and pier response over broadcast/mean fusion
contrast: SACNO versus FLOAT_TCN under both B0 and B1
risk: Coordinate proximity may not equal structural connectivity
pass_rule: At least 5% RMSE gain and stable pier metrics
innovation_claim: Possible: a sensor-availability-conditioned coordinate operator performs topology-aware sparse-to-full seismic field assimilation with an exact zero-sensor limit.

mechanism: One shared model decomposes the response into a ground-only prior field and a mask-gated sensor correction field and trains paired B0/B1 counterfactuals
compatibility: Exactly preserves matched architecture and exposes B0/B1 from one checkpoint
estimator_information: Same deployment information as B0 or B1
hypothesis: Joint paired supervision improves B0 stability and makes B1 correction reliably beneficial
contrast: Joint nested model versus separately trained matched models
risk: Ranking loss may suppress useful corrections or overfit validation behavior
pass_rule: B1 win rate >=65% and both modes competitive with separate models
innovation_claim: Possible: recast sparse-sensor reconstruction as an auditable prior-to-posterior field update within one nested operator rather than two unrelated networks.

mechanism: Combine robust waveform, temporal slope, spectral amplitude and peak losses in physical normalized space
compatibility: No extra deployment information; full output retained
estimator_information: Training truth only for supervised loss
hypothesis: Multi-domain supervision reduces spectral bias and peak shrinkage
contrast: NESTED_DUAL with and without composite loss
risk: Poor weights can destabilize training or overemphasize rare peaks
pass_rule: RMSE improvement with peak error non-degradation
innovation_claim: Preliminary candidate: multi-domain physical supervision targets the known amplitude-shrinkage failure of image GAN response reconstruction.

mechanism: Add low-cost multi-receptive-field temporal branches to the ground and sensor encoders while retaining coordinate graph propagation and the exact zero-sensor limit
compatibility: Full [B,3,153,1000] output; B0/B1 have identical architecture within the pair
estimator_information: Ground motion; sparse sensors and mask only when available
hypothesis: Multi-scale temporal receptive fields improve the sensor-free prior and preserve sensor-assisted corrections
contrast: MS_SACNO B0/B1 versus SACNO B0/B1 at matched budget
risk: More parameters and possible over-smoothing across frequencies
pass_rule: B0 nRMSE and peak error both improve without B1 regression
innovation_claim: Possible: a multi-scale temporal prior operator addresses the low-frequency/high-frequency mixture that limits sensor-free spatial response recovery.

mechanism: Use a small gradient-balanced peak-aware loss and include normalized peak relative error in model selection
compatibility: No deployment truth; peak target is used only during supervised training and post-hoc evaluation
estimator_information: Ground motion; sparse sensors and mask only when available
hypothesis: Peak-balanced supervision reduces acceleration peak attenuation without sacrificing global full-field nRMSE
contrast: PEAK_SACNO versus SACNO with identical architecture and data
risk: Peak emphasis can hurt waveform error or overfit rare records
pass_rule: Peak absolute error improves and nRMSE degradation <2%
innovation_claim: Preliminary: treat peak response as a first-class field objective rather than a secondary visual metric; prove with waveform/peak Pareto analysis.

mechanism: Multiply coordinate attention by a learned sensor-quality gate and train with normalized sensor noise and random sensor dropout
compatibility: Exact zero-mask correction remains zero; B0/B1 remain the same architecture and output
estimator_information: Only noisy sparse sensors and availability mask; no full-field truth
hypothesis: Quality gating improves robustness under sensor corruption while preserving clean full-field accuracy
contrast: QG_SACNO B0/B1 clean and stressed evaluation versus SACNO
risk: Quality gate may suppress useful but low-amplitude sensors or add variance
pass_rule: Stressed B1 peak and RMSE improve with clean B1 degradation <2%
innovation_claim: Possible: an availability- and quality-conditioned posterior correction converts sparse virtual sensing from an all-or-nothing assumption into a deployable sensor-health-aware operator.

mechanism: Use a sample-adaptive soft gate over short-, medium- and long-receptive-field temporal branches before coordinate graph propagation
compatibility: Same adaptive operator and output shape for B0/B1; gate uses only ground or available sensor windows
estimator_information: Ground motion; sparse sensors and mask only when available
hypothesis: Event-dependent scale selection should reduce fixed-receptive-field bias in mixed low/high-frequency seismic responses
contrast: AMS_SACNO versus fixed-scale SACNO/MS_SACNO under clean and stressed matched pairs
risk: The gate may collapse to one scale or overfit the small training set
pass_rule: Improves both B0 and B1 full-field nRMSE or gives a Pareto improvement in peak error without clean regression
innovation_claim: Candidate contribution: a sensor-availability-conditioned neural operator with sample-adaptive temporal scale selection for rapid full-field seismic response reconstruction.

mechanism: Combine fixed multi-scale temporal encoding with the gradient-balanced peak-aware objective
compatibility: No extra deployment information; B0/B1 share the same architecture and loss under each pair
estimator_information: Ground motion; sparse sensors and mask only when available
hypothesis: Separating temporal-scale representation from peak-risk supervision may improve both waveform and acceleration-peak recovery
contrast: MS_PEAK_SACNO versus MS_SACNO and PEAK_SACNO matched pairs
risk: Two improvements may interact non-additively and peak emphasis can degrade global error
pass_rule: Dominates the corresponding single-factor model on at least two of nRMSE, peak ARE and pier-top RMSE
innovation_claim: Candidate contribution: jointly optimize full-field waveform fidelity and extreme-response recovery within a single sparse-to-full operator.
